title: Cypher System
author: ThunderForgeVTT Contributors
description: Cypher System ruleset for ThunderForgeVTT, digested from its official SRD (see research/system_cypher_system.json for full provenance).

proficiencyTiers.description: Cypher System deliberately has no fixed skill list (per research/system_cypher_system.json's `skills` digest); a character's relationship to any given task is instead described by one of these training tiers, which ease or hinder the task's difficulty before the 1d20 roll (see `taskResolution`).

trained.label: Trained
trained.effect: Eases the task's difficulty by one step.

specialized.label: Specialized
specialized.effect: Eases the task's difficulty by two steps (the maximum from skill training alone).

practiced.label: Practiced
practiced.effect: The unmodified default — no ease or hindrance from training.

inability.label: Inability
inability.effect: Hinders the task's difficulty by one step; canceled out if the character is also trained in the same task.

taskResolution.description: The Cypher System's universal task-resolution mechanic: the GM sets a task's difficulty (1-10); the target number is always difficulty x 3. The player rolls 1d20 and succeeds if the result meets or beats the target number. Difficulty is eased (lowered) before the roll by skill training, assets, and Effort, and hindered (raised) by circumstance; a difficulty eased to 0 succeeds automatically with no roll.
taskResolution.notes: The dice-engine formula is a plain '1d20' roll (crates/thunderforge-dice's grammar only supports a success-threshold modifier like 'cs>={n}' with a literal numeric condition, not a placeholder-driven one, so a dynamic per-roll target number of 3x a variable difficulty cannot be expressed inside the formula string itself). The roll result is compared against the target number in application logic, not in the dice formula.
